messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — ran a long-context (32k) FP8 v2 vs INT8(calib) kernel sweep on a prod-like config. Observed a TTFT regression for FP8 prefill: ~210ms -> ~520ms with our 4-bit KV compress path. Anyone seen something similar?

liam: Hmm that is quite large. Are you on the new kernel-selection heuristic branch? Startup cost for some FP8 kernels is high; should be amortized for long prefill but your TTFT implies startup dominates. What's the batch size and hardware?

maya: batch=1, model=gpt-30b, H100-80GB (dedicated). Batching policy: continuous, dynamic_max_tokens=256. Repro command: 
```
./bench_prefill --model gpt-30b --quant fp8 --seq_len 32000 --batch 1 --kv-compress=4
```

maya: perf-bot: posting microbench numbers below :chart_with_upwards_trend: 

perf-bot: Microbench summary (abridged):
- Prefill TTFT (ms): FP8: 520, INT8(calib): 240, FP32: 480
- Decode steady-state TPS: FP8: 38 t/s, INT8: 35 t/s, FP32: 41 t/s
- KV write latency (prefill): FP8+4bit compress: +220ms vs no-compress

sofia: Interesting. My hunch: the INT8 calibration flow does offline scaling which allows using the int8_gemm that has lower startup overhead for prefill. Did you capture the kernel-selection log for the run?

maya: Pasted kernel-selection trace (snip):
```
[selector] seq_len=32000, batch=1, mode=prefill
[selector] candidate kernels: fp8_gemm_v2 (startup_cost=0.45, per_token=0.011), int8_gemm_calib (startup_cost=0.08, per_token=0.016), fp32_gemm (startup_cost=0.30, per_token=0.012)
[selector] chosen: fp8_gemm_v2 (score=... weighting startup=0.3, per_token=0.7)
```

kai: From that trace it looks like the selector still biases per_token cost moderately, but FP8's measured startup is worse than recorded in the profiler. Also note our KV compress/unpack path introduces a CPU->GPU unpack and an extra cudaMemcpy at prefill write time which isn't accounted for in the kernel startup metric.

jon: So two contributors: (1) KV compress/unpack overhead during prefill write, (2) selector weights and maybe stale startup metric for fp8_gemm_v2. We should confirm by toggling KV compress.

maya: Reran with --kv-compress=0: FP8 prefill TTFT -> 300ms (down from 520ms). So the compress/unpack adds ~220ms in prefill. Confirmed.

liam: That aligns. Compress helps reduce memory footprint and network egress, but it's paid at prefill write time. Decode streams are largely unaffected because decode writes small incremental KV updates. So TTFT vs TPS tradeoff: compress hurts TTFT but preserves long-run TPS/throughput and memory.

sofia: Two immediate ideas: (A) make KV compress unpack async and overlap with the kernel launch so unpack cost can be hidden; (B) tweak kernel selector rule: for prefill or seq_len>8192 bias toward lower startup kernels. We also need to re-run quality checks if we force int8 kernels for prefill.

perf-bot: Regression ticket created: perf/789 — after commit abc123 (fp8 kernel v2) we see 1.3x TTFT regression on longctx prefill. Canary job scheduled.

jon: I'll open a patch that forces int8_gemm for the prefill path when seq_len > 8192 and B=1 as an experiment (no default flip). We'll collect end-to-end latency + P99 and quality deltas on eval prompts.

maya: Also found that FP8 kernel's calibration stage (runtime micro-calib) does a host-side re-quantization pass for the KV tile layout which triggers several memcpy and temp allocations. Turning off runtime micro-calib reduces TTFT but may change output slightly.

kai: We should add selector telemetry: per-kernel startup measured (actual wallclock), memcpy counts, and whether KV compress was used. Add these to route-level logs for the next canary.

liam: For the performance matrix, run FP32/FP8/INT8(offline-calib)/4-bit-kv with seq_lens = [512, 2048, 8192, 32768], B=[1,4], and record TTFT, steady TPS, GPU util, and KV write time. Also capture per-kernel launch time and memcpy breakdown.

maya: I'll draft an RFC with the experiment plan and patch proposals: (1) async KV compress unpack, (2) temporary selector override for prefill->int8, (3) update FP8 startup cost from profiler and bump weight, (4) perf tests + canary.

sofia: One more note: we observed FP8 decode TPS ~38 vs FP32 41 — small gap, so FP8 is fine for throughput. The main user pain is TTFT for interactive UIs. We should consider a route-level knob to prefer lower TTFT for interactive endpoints (TTFT-SLO) vs maximize TPS for batch endpoints.

jon: Agreed. I'll wire route config: "latency_profile": ["ttft_prioritize", "throughput_prioritize"] and default to throughput.

perf-bot: Action items recorded: 1) perf/789 created, 2) canary + telemetry scheduled, 3) RFC branch opened.

maya: TL;DR: root cause = KV compress unpack + stale FP8 startup metric affecting kernel selector under long-context prefill (TTFT). Plan = async unpack + selector tweak + measured canary. I'll follow up with the RFC link and bench CSVs. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
